wilco_ec: Enable WILCO_EC kernel configs if enabled by USE flag To build kernel support for the Wilco Embedded Controller, we need some kernel configs set. However, we can't add them to the common .configs within the kernel, since doing so would break some other chromebooks. We need the configs set just for Wilco. Specifically, CONFIG_WILCO_EC depends upon CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC, but we can't enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC for all boards, since that would break all boards that don't use the Microchip EC. So for only Wilco we need to enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC and all the desired CONFIG_WILCO_* configs. A solution to this has already been similarly implemented for other boards, so that each board gets a custom config. Specifically, in src/overlays/baseboard-glados/profiles/base/make.defaults the cros_ec_mec USE flag is set. Then, in src/third_party/chromiumos-overlay/eclass/cros-kernel2.eclass, some kernel configs are modified when that use flag is set. This commit sets the kernel configs when the proper USE flag is set. At this point the configs are set to compile as modules. This is for development, in production we want to change the "m"s to "y"s BUG=b:124470322 TEST=manual: After applying CL:1474707 as well, the kernel builds with the wilco modules Change-Id: I5e9eb13cd7a6dc9cb03ecad1aaff45f51e1859ef Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1474254 Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: perf/core: Fix impossible ring-buffer sizes warning The following commit: 9dff0aa95a32 ("perf/core: Don't WARN() for impossible ring-buffer sizes") results in perf recording failures with larger mmap areas: root@skl:/tmp# perf record -g -a failed to mmap with 12 (Cannot allocate memory) The root cause is that the following condition is buggy: if (order_base_2(size) >= MAX_ORDER) goto fail; The problem is that @size is in bytes and MAX_ORDER is in pages, so the right test is: if (order_base_2(size) >= PAGE_SHIFT+MAX_ORDER) goto fail; Fix it. Reported-by: "Jin, Yao" <yao.jin@linux.intel.com> Bisected-by: Borislav Petkov <bp@alien8.de> Analyzed-by: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org> Cc: Julien Thierry <julien.thierry@arm.com> Cc: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com> Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com> Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@redhat.com> Cc: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@redhat.com> Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> Cc: Namhyung Kim <namhyung@kernel.org> Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org> Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de> Cc: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> Fixes: 9dff0aa95a32 ("perf/core: Don't WARN() for impossible ring-buffer sizes") Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 528871b456026e6127d95b1b2bd8e3a003dc1614) BUG=b:124795843 TEST=perf record -g -a Change-Id: I418f2b70c3de76d0c59e7f278107eba4b5d80ba2 Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1478049 Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu Zhao <yuzhao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alexey Alexandrov <aalexand@google.com>

grpc: Fix vsock patch The vsock code in the kernel checks that an undocumented `svm_zero` field in the sockaddr_vm struct is always set to 0. To do this, we have to allocated the sockaddr_vm struct with gpr_zalloc, which will zero out the entire structure. Fix the vsock patch to do that. hermes: qmi_uim: Update qmi_uim files with qmi2cpp Prior to this CL, the qmi_uim.{h,cc} files were only loosely based on the qmi_uim.qmi file. The qmic tool generated some code that had to be modified by hand before being ready for use with hermes. This is unfortunate, as many future additions to hermes functionality requires adding support for more QMI messages. This led to the creation of qmi2cpp, which is a python program that uses the same (almost) qmi specification file to generate exactly the code we need. This change updates the qmi_uim.qmi file for use with qmi2cpp and regenerates qmi_uim.{h,cc} from scratch. No changes to functionality were made here. This CL serves primarily to ensure that using qmi2cpp does not break any existing functionality. BUG=chromium:847619 TEST=Existing functionality working as before. Change-Id: Ib0076a46ae6a9d6e0516cc2807dcce8afd8ae09a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1368988 Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: virtwl: fix dma_buf_get() retval handling dma_buf_get() doesn't return NULL on failure; instead, it returns an error-valued pointer. The old code dereferenced such error-valued pointers, causing the kernel to oops with a near-NULL pointer dereference when passed a file descriptor of unexpected type. Fix it by checking for error-valued pointers instead of NULL, and also pass through the error code dma_buf_get() gives us instead of always using -EINVAL. BUG=chromium:933011 TEST=kernel-crashing test program crashes no more Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com> Change-Id: I296e182c9b4412a5e79e7109abce376436ebe472 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1477256 Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

power/intel_x86: Do not restore SCI/SMI masks if not backed up Currently, if the host indicates intent to enter S0ix using host command but fails to drop into S0ix (i.e. assert SLP_S0#), then it results in EC not backing up SCI/SMI masks. However, SCI/SMI masks were being unconditionally restored when host sent command to exit S0ix. This resulted in failed S0ix to wipe out the SCI mask. This change skips restoring SCI/SMI masks if backup masks are zero. BUG=b:124540202 BRANCH=None TEST=Ensured that with S0ix failure, SCI mask was not wiped out. Change-Id: Ia79829b616ebff460e2436b03653f74aaf6c1ba0 Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1476291 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Scott Collyer <scollyer@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org>
